Definition: middle voice of a primary verb; to wish; by implication, to pray to God:--pray, will, wish.
BiblicalUsage: Eúchomai means to wish — and by extension, to pray, to ask God for what you wish. Paul wishes the Corinthians would be perfect, and James says to pray one for another, that ye may be healed. It is the word for the heart's wish turned toward God in prayer.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe eúchomai shows that prayer starts with wishing — with wanting something enough to ask God for it. I hold that praying for one another is not fancy words, but a plain wish laid before God.
